messages.body_plain:
Le mer. 22 mai 2019 à 01:32, Jeroen Ooms <jeroen at berkeley.edu> a écrit :

> Hi Jérémy
>
>
>
> Now that r-cran-v8 seems to be working great with libnode-dev, perhaps
>
> the old libv8 should be removed from sid?  Today I was working in sid
>
> and I noticed that apt still prefers the old v8 over the libnode-dev
>
> virtual package when installing libv8-dev as a dependency.
>
>
>
> Alternatively, instead of removing the old libv8 alltogether, you
>
> could push a mini-update for the old package such that libv8-3.14-dev
>
> no longer provides libv8-dev, but libv8-3.14-dev keeps existing in
>
> sid. Thereby there will only be one libv8-dev in sid, which is the
>
> libnode-dev virtual package. However if people really want the old
>
> package for whatever reason, they could still install libv8-3.14-dev.

Thanks for the tip, i'll do that !

Jérémy

so i'd rather remove libv8-3.14 entirely.

messages.subject: Backports for Stretch updated
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I've updated all upgradable r-cran-* and r-bioc-* packages that were
once backported to Stretch to the latest version in Buster.  There are
two exceptions:  r-cran-effects (4.0.1 is backported, 4.1.0 is in
Buster) and r-cran-stanheaders (2.17.2 is backported, 2.18.1 is in
Buster).  The reason for the two not updated ones is that these
explicitly require a higher version of r-base than we have currently in
Stretch.  I'm not interested to backport r-base since when I tried the
shiny application we are using here did not worked.  So my main
motivation to keep packages backported properly was spoiled for this
one.

Just to keep you informed about the backport status

      Andreas.

-- 
http://fam-tille.de
